displayNameCn: 伍麦叶·本·阿卜杜·沙姆斯
fullNameCn: 伍麦叶·本·阿卜杜·沙姆斯

events.label: Became the eponymous ancestor of Banū Umayya
events.labelCn: 成为伍麦叶家族的名祖
events.note: Classical genealogy identifies Umayya as the ancestor after whom Banū Umayya was named.

events.label: Was later associated with a rivalry with Hāshim
events.labelCn: 后世传统将其与哈希姆的竞争联系起来
events.note: Later narratives describe rivalry and arbitration between Umayya and Hāshim, but these stories are shaped by later Hashimite-Umayyad political memory.

sourceNote: Ibn Isḥāq/Ibn Hishām; al-Balādhurī, Ansāb al-ashrāf; al-Ṭabarī; G. R. Hawting; Wikipedia as supplementary index.
notes:
Eponymous ancestor of Banū Umayya and the bridge to Ḥarb and Abū Sufyān.

Confidence / caveats: Stories of rivalry and exile are later traditions and difficult to separate from Abbasid-era polemic. No secure birth or death year is available.

Unlinked family: child: Abū al-ʿĀṣ ibn Umayya

events.label: Was remembered as a leading notable of Banū Umayya
events.labelCn: 被记载为伍麦叶支的重要贵族领袖
events.note: Later Arabic tradition places Ḥarb among prominent pre-Islamic Banū Umayya leaders.

events.label: Fathered Abū Sufyān
events.note: Through Abū Sufyān, Ḥarb became paternal grandfather of Muʿāwiya I.

sourceNote: Ibn Ḥabīb; al-Balādhurī; al-Ṭabarī; G. R. Hawting; Wikipedia as stable index.
notes:
Main project value is genealogical: Umayya → Ḥarb → Abū Sufyān → Muʿāwiya I.

Confidence / caveats: Very little can be anchored securely in absolute chronology; Fijār-war anecdotes and leadership stories are not converted into precise dates.

deathCause.summary: Killed by rebels during the siege of his house in Medina
deathCause.summaryCn: 麦地那居所遭围攻时被叛乱者杀害
deathCause.detail: Rebels entered his house after a prolonged siege and killed him; accounts differ over the individual assailants and exact sequence.
deathCause.detailCn: 长期围困后，叛乱者进入其宅邸并将其杀害；关于具体行刺者与过程的记载并不一致。

events.label: Became an early Muslim convert
events.labelCn: 成为早期穆斯林皈依者
events.note: Tradition identifies ʿUthmān among the early converts in Mecca.

events.label: Joined the migration to Abyssinia
events.note: He and Ruqayya, Muhammad’s daughter, were among the early emigrants in Islamic tradition.

events.label: Migrated to Medina
events.note: He became a member of the Medinan Muslim community.

events.label: Was chosen as the third caliph
events.labelCn: 获推举为第三任哈里发
events.note: A council appointed by ʿUmar chose ʿUthmān after ʿUmar’s death.

events.label: Authorized campaigns in North Africa
events.labelCn: 批准在北非的军事行动
events.note: Rashidun forces expanded westward into former Byzantine Africa during his reign.

events.label: Authorized the first Muslim naval expedition to Cyprus
events.labelCn: 批准首次穆斯林海军远征塞浦路斯
events.note: The campaign marked a major extension of Rashidun military capacity at sea.

events.label: Commissioned a standard written recension of the Qurʾan
events.labelCn: 主持形成《古兰经》的标准书面定本
events.note: The Uthmanic recension became the canonical consonantal text in Sunni tradition.

events.label: Rashidun fleet defeated Byzantium at the Battle of the Masts
events.labelCn: 正统哈里发舰队在桅杆之战中击败拜占庭
events.note: The naval victory challenged Byzantine dominance in the eastern Mediterranean.

events.label: Was killed during the siege of his house in Medina
events.labelCn: 麦地那居所遭围攻时遇害
events.note: His death triggered the First Fitna, the first major civil war of the caliphate.

sourceNote: Hugh N. Kennedy, The Prophet and the Age of the Caliphates; Fred M. Donner, Muhammad and the Believers; Wikipedia used as a chronology index.
notes:
Third caliph of the Rashidun period. His recension of the Qurʾan and his violent death were decisive for the later political and religious history of Islam.

Confidence / caveats: conventional birth year is approximate; accounts of the siege and individual attackers differ substantially between later sources.
